steps: Spread both hands into open fives with fingers wide apart in front of your torso.
Hold both hands at chest height with your palms turned to face you.
Push both hands upward in a flickering motion, raising and lowering them alternately.
Wiggle all ten fingers as the hands rise, like flames licking upward.
Keep your expression neutral; the quick finger wiggle sells the motion of fire.
tip: The flickering, wiggling fingers are the giveaway — without them the sign reads as a plain raise.

steps: Tap the fingers of a W handshape against your chin to sign WATER first.
Hold both flat hands in neutral space with fingers pointing forward.
Turn both palms to face each other, about a foot apart.
Sweep both hands forward together in a curvy side-to-side zigzag.
Keep the zigzag smooth and continuous, picturing a winding stream flowing onward.
tip: The curvy zigzag is the river's path; straight fingers moving forward would read like a flat road.

steps: Hold both hands open and relaxed, fingers together and slightly spread.
Place both hands out in front of your waist, side by side.
Turn your palms down and let them face the floor.
Move both hands up and down in small rolling waves, pushing slightly forward.
Keep the two hands moving in sync, like twin swells rolling under them.
tip: Think of your hands riding two waves — the same sign covers SEA, OCEAN, and breaking waves.

steps: Plant your non-dominant elbow near your waist and raise that forearm upright like a trunk.
Open your dominant hand into a five with fingers spread wide.
Rest the wrist of the open five on top of the upright forearm.
Twist the open hand left and right twice from the wrist.
Keep the forearm steady and upright so it reads as the tree trunk.
tip: The trunk arm stays still while only the hand twists — two quick twists, no more.

steps: Open your dominant hand into a relaxed five, fingers together and thumb out.
Bring the hand up beside one cheek, fingertips near your temple.
Sweep the open hand in a wide circle around your face, ending beside the other cheek.
Keep your palm facing inward toward your face through the whole circle.
Smile warmly and lift your cheeks — the pleased face completes the meaning.
tip: The smiling face does half the work; a neutral face behind the circle weakens the meaning.

steps: Hold both flat hands up at neck height, fingers together.
Keep the hands a few inches apart on either side of your neck.
Bend both wrists so the fingertips flap inward toward your throat twice.
Turn both palms to face inward toward you as the hands flap.
Purse your lips slightly or raise your eyebrows to add an approving vibe.
tip: Two crisp wrist flaps mean COOL; slow it down and it reads as fanning yourself from heat.

steps: Close both hands into fists and tap your dominant fist on top of the other twice to sign ROCK.
Open both hands and raise them upward in front of your chest.
Stack the hands with one above the other, the higher hand near your forehead.
Turn both palms to face away from you as you lift.
Look up slightly as the hands rise, showing the great height of the peak.
tip: ROCK plus the rising stack — skip the rock tap and signers may read it as plain TALL.

steps: Open both hands into fives with fingers spread, held at chest height.
Hold the hands apart in front of your torso, palms facing inward toward you.
Sweep both hands downward toward your waist in one smooth motion.
Curl your fingers into claw shapes as the hands descend, as if night is closing in.
Lower your eyebrows or dim your expression to match the fading light.
tip: The 5-to-claw change is the key beat — flat hands sinking straight down reads as a different sign.

steps: Form the sign for TREE: forearm upright as trunk, open five twisted twice on top.
Extend your non-dominant forearm horizontally in front of your chest.
Set the tree handshape near your wrist at the far end of that forearm.
Slide the tree handshape sideways along the top of the forearm to the elbow.
Keep your face relaxed; the repeated sliding tree tells the whole story.
tip: Sliding the tree along the arm marks many trees — a single twist just says TREE.

steps: Open both hands into relaxed fives with fingers slightly spread.
Hold the hands out in front of your shoulders, a foot apart.
Turn both palms to face each other across the gap.
Sweep both hands sideways together, then back, repeating the motion twice.
Puff your cheeks or blow gently to sell the breeze with your face.
tip: The cheeks do half the work — still, flat hands drifting sideways without them read as plain air.

steps: Curl both hands into stiff claws, fingers hooked and spread apart.
Hold the clawed hands in front of your chest, a few inches apart.
Pull both hands sharply inward toward your body in one quick jerk.
Turn both palms down as the hands snap back toward you.
Tense your shoulders and freeze your face, as if the cold has seized you.
tip: The sudden inward snap reads as freezing over — a slow squeeze just looks like grabbing.

steps: Close both hands into S fists, thumbs resting on the curled fingers.
Hold both fists up at chest height, a few inches apart.
Push both fists outward to the sides, then pull them back toward the middle.
Repeat the out-and-in motion twice, keeping both forearms fairly still.
Hunch your shoulders slightly and pull a chilly face to match the shiver.
tip: Keep the S fists moving side to side — moving them up and down collides with the sign CAR.

steps: Touch the fingertips of your O handshape to the corner of your mouth.
This opening move borrows the EAT sign for where meals happen.
Slide the same O handshape upward to rest against your cheekbone.
The cheek touch borrows SLEEP, where rest happens each night.
Keep the motion smooth and unhurried, like settling into your own rooms.
tip: Mouth then cheek equals EAT plus SLEEP — together they spell out the idea of HOME.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand open and flat at waist height, palm facing up, like an open book.
Form an A fist with your dominant hand, thumb pressed against the knuckles.
Raise the dominant fist over the open hand and flick the thumb upward.
Sweep the raised thumb sideways across the open palm, as if flipping a page over.
Keep your gaze on the open hand, as if reading the page you just turned.
tip: The thumb is the turning page — swipe it the other way and the page turns backward.

steps: Curve your dominant hand into a C, thumb and fingers forming a claw.
Raise the C hand to the middle of your face, beside your nose.
Circle the C hand clockwise around the center of your face.
Turn the palm to face left (if right-handed) as the hand orbits.
Squint slightly or scan your eyes around, as if hunting for something.
tip: The C orbits the face clockwise — a C circling anywhere else reads as a different sign.

steps: Form the letter W with your dominant hand, three fingers spread and thumb tucked.
Hold the W up at chest height in neutral space in front of you.
Produce the W handshape twice in quick succession, resetting between forms.
Turn your palm to face forward during each of the two Ws.
Keep your face neutral; this technical sign carries no special expression.
tip: Two crisp Ws at chest height mean website — add a third and it is no longer this sign.

steps: Open your dominant hand into a five, fingers together and thumb relaxed.
Slide the open hand under your non-dominant flat hand at waist height.
Draw the dominant hand outward and upward from beneath the other hand.
Close the fingers into a flat O as the hand emerges from underneath.
Start with the dominant palm down, letting it rotate as it exits.
tip: As a standalone it means OUT; inside a sentence it usually folds into a classifier verb.

steps: Close your dominant hand into an A fist, thumb resting against the knuckles.
Hold the A fist up at chest height in neutral space.
Start with the palm facing sideways toward your non-dominant side.
Twist the wrist smoothly so the palm finishes facing the floor.
Keep your eyebrows raised slightly, marking it as an open, indefinite offer.
tip: The palm-down twist is the whole sign — hold it sideways and it reads as unfinished.
